capabilities.target: CI container on a shared runner, full process access
any repository in the GitHub org (ORG_WIDE_PAT scope)
.agent/config.yaml: controls model, autonomy, max_steps, tools, network

inputs.source: GitHub issue title and body, labeled "bug", public repo, any user can create via issue template
Repository file contents (code, tests, configs) read while reproducing and fixing the bug

instructions.note: "Pick up any issue labeled bug and fix it end to end" lets any user-labeled issue drive an autonomous, irreversible pipeline (shell exec, push, PR) with no scoping of which issues or repos are in-bounds.
The only stated control against destructive or exfiltrating commands is a natural-language instruction, with no structural enforcement such as an egress allowlist or a destructive-command denylist.

The agent's entire declared defense against indirect prompt injection from issue text or repository code is a single instruction to ignore embedded instructions; there is no spotlighting, delimiting, or input classifier.

Line 5 tells the agent to ignore instructions embedded in issues or code, but line 6 authorizes the same agent to self-modify .agent/config.yaml whenever it judges more tools are needed, a judgment an attacker-controlled issue can steer without ever being parsed as a direct instruction.

controls.name: Prompt instruction forbidding destructive or exfiltrating commands
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply; a more capable or longer-running model rationalizes exceptions or splits the forbidden action into allowed-looking steps.

controls.name: Prompt instruction to ignore instructions embedded in issues or code
controls.decay_rationale: Spotlighting by instruction only; works only if the model respects the boundary, and adaptive injected prompts close the gap as capability grows.

controls.name: Execution inside a CI container
controls.decay_rationale: Isolates the filesystem from the host, but the runner has unrestricted outbound network and the shell holds a broad org-wide credential, so it does not meaningfully constrain egress or credential misuse even today.

controls.name: Per-repository least-privilege GitHub token instead of an org-wide PAT
controls.decay_rationale: A token scoped to only the target repo, without workflow scope, would prevent cross-repo pivoting and does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Network egress allowlist for the CI container
controls.decay_rationale: Restricting outbound destinations to known package registries and the git remote would sever most exfiltration paths; currently network is unrestricted.

controls.name: Human approval before branch push/PR and before any self-config change
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action human approval gate on push and self-config would independently block unreviewed exfiltration or privilege escalation; none exists today (autonomy: full, no approval step declared).

controls.name: Immutable or out-of-band agent configuration (exclude .agent/ from fs.write)
controls.decay_rationale: Excluding .agent/ from the agent's own write scope would make self-reconfiguration structurally impossible regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted issue drives confidential read plus unrestricted egress

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled issue body/title; any GitHub user can add the bug label.
Agent reproduces/tests by running arbitrary shell commands that can read env secrets (ORG_WIDE_PAT) and reach the unrestricted network.
Alternative or parallel egress: push a branch/PR to a reachable repo, exposing data or secrets.

findings.residual_rationale: The container control would mechanically earn a step-3 credit, but it does not narrow this path because network egress is unrestricted and the shell carries a broad org-wide credential; only the two dependent prompt instructions (step 4, capped at -1) provide real protection, so residual is held at high rather than the lower tier the mechanical credit would produce.

forecast.watch_signal: model: latest auto-upgrades without review in .agent/config.yaml; watch for model version bumps or rising median steps/runtime per task.

evidence.observation: Agent autonomously picks up any bug-labeled issue, reproduces and tests via shell, and pushes/opens a PR with no human checkpoint.
autonomy: full, max_steps: null, network: unrestricted, and GITHUB_TOKEN is an org-wide PAT available to shell.run.
Any GitHub user can open issues and add the bug label through an issue template, making in.issue_body fully untrusted and attacker reachable.

recommendations.action: Add a network egress allowlist to the CI container restricting outbound destinations to package registries and the git remote.
Replace the org-wide PAT with a short-lived, repo-scoped token with no workflow scope.
Require raw-action human approval before github.push_branch/open_pr executes.

findings.title: Self-modification (TC3): untrusted issue can steer the agent's own tool/autonomy config

attack_path.note: Attacker crafts an issue implying the fix needs an additional tool or broader permission.
Agent edits .agent/config.yaml per prompt line 6, potentially adding tools, widening network access, or raising autonomy, persisting into future sessions.

forecast.watch_signal: Diff .agent/config.yaml over time; watch for tools, autonomy, network, or model fields changing without a human-reviewed commit.

evidence.observation: "You may adjust .agent/config.yaml if you need extra tools to finish a task" grants the model authority to change its own tool list, autonomy, network, and model fields.
The same file controls autonomy, max_steps, tools, and network, so one self-edit can remove every other declared constraint.

recommendations.action: Remove .agent/ from the agent's own fs.write scope; route tool or permission change requests to a human-reviewed PR instead.
Add integrity monitoring and alerting on changes to .agent/config.yaml.

findings.title: Confused deputy (ASI03): single-repo task holds an org-wide credential

attack_path.note: Shell can read the GITHUB_TOKEN env var, which is an org-wide PAT with repo + workflow scope.
Token scope lets a push reach repositories and CI workflows beyond the one repo with the triggering issue.

forecast.watch_signal: PAT scope widened, workflow scope retained, or additional org repos onboarded to the same token without re-review.

evidence.observation: env.GITHUB_TOKEN is bound to ${ORG_WIDE_PAT}; comment states repo + workflow scope on all org repos.
The agent is scoped to fix a single repo's bug issue but holds a credential valid across the entire organization, far beyond the task's needs.

recommendations.action: Mint a repo-scoped installation token per run instead of a static org-wide PAT; drop workflow scope entirely.

findings.title: Forecast: planned Slack MCP server adds an uncontrolled exfiltration channel (ASI02/ASI04)

attack_path.note: Agent reads confidential data (code, secrets) from the repo/environment while handling the issue.
Planned Slack MCP server (not yet built) would give a new, currently undescribed egress channel for posting that data.

forecast.watch_signal: A Slack MCP server entry appears in tool/MCP config; check whether it ships with defined scope, pinned tool definitions, and output filtering before it is enabled.

evidence.observation: "The team wants to add a Slack MCP server next quarter" — a new egress channel is planned with no described authentication, pinning, or scoping yet.

recommendations.action: Before connecting the Slack MCP server, pin tool definitions, scope the Slack token to a single notifications channel, and add output filtering so posted content cannot include secrets or repo contents.

rating.rationale: Every present finding reaches an S3 sink (irreversible execute/push/configure, or confidential egress) from an untrusted source (any GitHub user via the bug label), giving critical inherent risk across the board. The only declared controls are two behavioral, capability-dependent prompt instructions plus a container that does not meaningfully narrow the path given unrestricted network and a broad org-wide credential; applying the rubric's step-4 cap holds residual at high. Under model_upgrade or longer_task_horizon, the one real credit (the dependent prompt instructions) is expected to fail, returning every finding to critical, and the planned Slack MCP server would add a new uncontrolled egress channel under new_mcp_server. The forecast is driven most by the pair of prompt-only instructions (ctrl.no_exfil_instruction, ctrl.ignore_injected_instructions), which are the sole protection against goal hijack, self-reconfiguration, and credential misuse.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, .agent/config.yaml, and the provided runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool-call schema, GitHub App manifest, or actual token-scope documentation was provided beyond the config.yaml comment; credential_scope and is_egress classifications for cap.shell and cap.git_push are inferred and may differ from the real deployed scope.

The Slack MCP server is only described as a future plan with no configuration; cap.slack_mcp and the corresponding forecast finding are speculative and must be re-assessed once an actual MCP config exists.
